manifest.name: To-Do
manifest.summary: Organize your work with memos and to-do lists
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Create activity and todo at the same time
Task (inherit; turns project.task into the To-Do object when project_id is empty)
models.note: Adds no fields - a To-Do is simply a project.task with project_id=False, parent_id=False, assigned to the user. Overrides create() for auto-naming and adds the convert-to-task action and the To-Do view-id lookup.

models._description: User (inherit; splits to-do vs task activities in the systray and seeds onboarding to-dos)

security.note: 4 ir.model.access rows grant base.group_user CRUD on project.task.type, project.task (access_task_on_partner), project.tags, and read/write/create on the mail.activity.todo.create wizard (no unlink). The single ir.rule task_edition_rule_internal (noupdate, on project.model_project_task, group base.group_user) is the privacy gate: domain [('project_id','=',False),('user_ids','in',user.id),('parent_id','=',False)] - i.e. every internal user has FULL access to their own private, top-level, project-less tasks (to-dos), making to-dos personal by default. Defines no new groups; reuses project's.

views.note: All views are on project.task (or the wizard). Distinct js_class views: project_task_view_todo_kanban (default_group_by personal_stage_type_id, quick_create), project_task_view_todo_tree (todo_list, editable bottom, todo_done_checkmark), project_task_view_todo_form (todo_form, breadcrumb name edit + todo_chatter_panel), a quick-create form (parses #tags/@user/! priority shortcuts), project_task_view_todo_conversion_form (todo_conversion_form, project_id required). The main act_window project_task_action_todo hard-codes domain [('user_ids','in',[uid]),('project_id','=',False),('parent_id','=',False)] and context default_project_id=False, path 'to-do'. A second act_window project_task_action_convert_todo_to_task opens the conversion form target=new.

behavioral_notes.observation: Overrides @api.model_create_multi create(). For any vals with NO name AND NO project_id AND NO parent_id (i.e. a bare private to-do), it derives a title from the description: html2plaintext(description), strip, drop '*', take the first line (partition('\n')[0]), truncate to 97 chars + '...' if over 100; if there is no description it falls back to _('Untitled to-do'). So a to-do typed straight into the description editor gets its breadcrumb name auto-generated - a behaviour no metadata exposes, and one that is scoped precisely to the project-less/parentless to-do case so real project tasks are unaffected.

The promotion path. ensure_one(); sets self.company_id = self.project_id.company_id then returns an ir.actions.act_window opening the same record (res_id=self.id) in form view. The to-do becomes a normal project task simply because the conversion form (project_task_view_todo_conversion_form, opened by the TodoFormController 'Convert to Task' cog item only when the user has project.group_project_user and the record has no project_id yet) makes project_id required - once a project_id is written, the task leaves the to-do domain ([('project_id','=',False)]) and gains its project stage/company. No data copy or new record: conversion is an in-place re-scoping of one project.task from personal to project-owned.

behavioral_notes.element: res.users._get_activity_groups (systray To-Do/Task split via raw SQL)
behavioral_notes.observation: Overrides the activity systray builder. It removes the single aggregated project.task activity group, then runs a raw SQL CTE over mail_activity JOIN project_task for the current user that buckets each task by BOOL(t.project_id) AS is_task (True = real task, False = to-do) and by today/overdue/planned (computed from MIN(date_deadline) vs today), counting max one activity per task. It then rebuilds TWO systray groups - 'To-Do' (is_todo=True, icon from the project_todo manifest) and 'Task' (icon from project) - each with total/today/overdue/planned counts and a domain ['activity_ids.res_id','in', res_ids]. This is why the activity menu shows To-Do and Task as separate stacks though both are project.task; the split is SQL-driven and invisible to metadata.

The module's post_init_hook _todo_post_init calls env['res.users'].search([('share','=',False)])._generate_onboarding_todo(), and _onboard_users_into_project is overridden so newly onboarded users also get one. _generate_onboarding_todo renders the QWeb template 'project_todo.todo_user_onboarding' per user (in the user's lang), titles it _('Welcome %s!', user.name), and creates a project.task with_user(SUPERUSER_ID) and context mail_auto_subscribe_no_notify=True carrying user_ids=user.ids, description=rendered body, name=title - i.e. every non-portal user is seeded a private welcome to-do on install/onboarding, silently (no notification). A pure side-effect of install, not a field.

The 'Add a To-Do' wizard (4 fields: summary, required date_deadline default today, user_id default current user readonly, Html note). create_todo_activity() creates a project.task (name=summary, description=note, date_deadline, user_ids=user_id) AND a mail.activity on that task (res_model_id=project.task, summary, user_id, date_deadline, activity_type_id = the model's default activity type), then returns a display_notification 'Your to-do has been successfully added to your pipeline.' So one wizard submit yields both a private to-do record and a scheduled activity pointing at it - dual side-effect not derivable from the 4 transient fields.

14 JS files, 1 OWL widget (TodoChatterPanel - a toggleable side chatter driven by a 'TODO:TOGGLE_CHATTER' bus event), 6 registry adds, and one patch ActivityMenu.prototype. The ActivityMenu patch adds an 'Add a To-Do' command (hotkey alt+shift+t) that ORM-creates the mail.activity.todo.create wizard and opens it in a FormViewDialog, and routes is_todo systray groups to To-Do-specific views fetched via project.task.get_todo_views_id (kanban/list/form/calendar/activity xml_ids). The to-do kanban/list/calendar group by personal_stage_type_id (project's per-user project.task.stage.personal relation) rather than a project stage_id - the mechanism that lets project-less to-dos still have draggable columns. The todo_done_checkmark field widget and todo_form/todo_list/todo_conversion_form js_class views complete the dedicated To-Do UI; the conversion form controller just autofocuses the project field.

it_architecture.application: project_todo (personal To-Do app; auto-installed productivity layer on top of project, reusing project.task)
logical_data_erm: project.task -> project.task.type via project.task.stage.personal (personal_stage_type_id, per-user kanban stage)
ir.rule task_edition_rule_internal -> project.task (own private project-less top-level tasks)
information_flows: depends: project (inherits project.task, personal stages, activity mixin, chatter)
side-effect: create project.task with no name/project/parent -> name auto-derived from description first line (or 'Untitled to-do')
side-effect: action_convert_to_task -> set company from chosen project, write project_id (required in conversion form) -> task exits the to-do domain and becomes a project task
side-effect: res.users._get_activity_groups -> raw SQL splits mail_activity on project.task into To-Do (no project) vs Task systray stacks
side-effect: mail.activity.todo.create.create_todo_activity -> creates one project.task + one mail.activity
install/onboarding: _todo_post_init / _generate_onboarding_todo -> seeds a 'Welcome' private to-do per non-share user (SUPERUSER_ID, no notify)
frontend: ActivityMenu patch -> 'Add a To-Do' command + to-do-specific systray views via get_todo_views_id

capabilities: Capture Personal To-Dos / Memos (private by default)
Auto-title a To-Do from its content
Track To-Dos through Personal Kanban Stages
Split To-Do vs Task Activities in the Systray
Create a To-Do together with a scheduled Activity
Promote (Convert) a Private To-Do into a shared Project Task
Onboard new users with a starter To-Do
value_streams: Personal-task lifecycle: capture a private to-do (type/quick-create/wizard) -> auto-name + assign to self -> organise by personal stage / deadline / tags -> mark done (todo_done_checkmark) or, when it becomes collaborative, convert into a project task and hand off to Project delivery
information_concepts: project.task (as a private To-Do when project_id is empty)
mail.activity (the scheduled reminder on a to-do)
organization: base.group_user (every internal user - to-dos are a universal personal feature, no dedicated group)
policies: Privacy policy (ir.rule task_edition_rule_internal): a user has full access only to their own project-less, top-level tasks; to-dos are private by default and shared by adding assignees
To-Do identity policy: project_id=False AND parent_id=False defines a to-do (vs a project task); writing a project_id converts it
Auto-naming policy: nameless project-less to-dos are titled from the description or 'Untitled to-do'
Onboarding policy: non-share users are seeded a Welcome to-do on install/onboarding (silently, as superuser)
stakeholders: Internal user / employee (owns and works their personal to-dos)
Assignee (additional res.users a to-do is shared with)
Project member (recipient when a to-do is converted to a project task)
metrics: systray to-do counts: total_count / today_count / overdue_count / planned_count (from _get_activity_groups)
open vs closed to-dos (is_closed filters in the to-do search view)

classification.apqc_category: 5.0 Deliver Services (personal task / to-do management layered on the Project value shop; a private project.task reused for personal-productivity / workforce enablement)
classification.rationale: project_todo inherits Project's value-SHOP DNA (it literally reuses project.task, personal kanban stages, the activity mixin and chatter - the same intensive-technology, organise-resources-around-each-problem model). A to-do is just a project.task with no project_id, moved through personal stages and optionally promoted into a real project task (action_convert_to_task), so the value-model is shop by inheritance. Activity class, however, is SUPPORT, not primary: this is a personal-productivity / self-organisation utility for the workforce, not a customer-facing delivery engine - it generates no revenue document, has no portal/customer surface, and is auto_install + universal (base.group_user). It enables employees to organise their own work (capture, remind via mail.activity, track, then hand off to Project), which is firm-infrastructure/workforce enablement. APQC maps to 5.0 Deliver Services, consistent with its parent project and the whole project_* family (all shop / 5.0): the concrete object IS a project.task moving through (personal) stages - the same intensive-technology service engine applied to an individual's own work. A 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital reading (personal task & productivity management for staff) and a 13.0 Develop & Manage Business Capabilities reading (the generic 'productivity tooling' bucket) were both weighed, but rejected in favour of inheriting Project's 5.0 anchor: project_todo adds no HR-function nor capability-building of its own - it is Project's task engine reused for private to-dos. Hence shop / support / 5.0.

standard_capabilities: private personal to-dos backed by project.task (project_id=False), private-by-default via record rule
quick-create with #tags/@user/! priority shortcuts; auto-naming from description
personal kanban / list / calendar / activity views grouped by per-user personal stage
mark-as-done checkmark widget and version history on the to-do description
'Add a To-Do' wizard that also schedules a mail.activity; systray To-Do/Task split
convert a to-do into a shared project task (sets project + company)
starter to-do seeded for new users on install/onboarding
typical_fits: employees keeping a personal task/memo list inside Odoo instead of a separate app
turning a self-note into team work by converting it to a project task once it needs collaboration
reminder-style activities created alongside the to-do (deadline + assignee)
any internal user (auto-installed, no configuration, no extra group)
common_gaps: no own reporting/analytics (pivot/graph) on to-dos - it borrows project's task analytics only after conversion
to-do is single-level (parent_id must be False) - no subtask hierarchy on personal to-dos
sharing is all-or-nothing via assignees; no granular per-collaborator permissions like project portal sharing
conversion is one-way and in-place (no template/recurrence applied on convert); onboarding to-do template is fixed
depends entirely on project being installed (auto_install) - cannot run standalone

Whether converting a to-do with existing assignees/tags merges cleanly with the target project's tag domain (conversion form scopes tags by project_id).
How get_todo_views_id view ids interact with the standard project.task systray when both project and project_todo activities exist for the same user.
